items.t: Pfizer in-licenses three preclinical in vivo CAR-T programs from Starna, with $330M upfront
items.ms: $330 million upfront, plus up to $2.3 billion in milestones and royalties on net sales.
items.why: On November 18, 2026, Pfizer obtained exclusive rights to develop, manufacture and commercialize three of Starna's preclinical in vivo CAR-T programs for autoimmune disease outside Greater China, together with rights to apply the technology in inflammation, immunology and oncology, and an option to expand the licensed territory into Greater China. Pfizer will lead clinical development outside Greater China and plans to manufacture initial clinical trial material at a U.S. site.
items.author: InLight Editorial

items.t: Spruce splits Harbour-originated CRHX-101 into Adrenyx, targeting a first-half 2027 Nasdaq listing
items.ms: Adrenyx has received an initial $5 million convertible note with a potential principal cap of $10 million, and plans a private placement at spin-out in which that investor may provide up to $50 million, including conversion. The 2025 license has a potential total value of up to $395 million.
items.why: On November 17, 2026, Harbour BioMed said partner Spruce Biosciences is separating the Harbour-originated antibody CRHX-101 (also known as SPR-202 / HBM9013) into a new wholly owned subsidiary, Adrenyx, which plans a Nasdaq listing in the first half of 2027. CRHX-101 is an anti-CRH monoclonal antibody in development for classic congenital adrenal hyperplasia. Near-term work includes IND-enabling studies and an FDA IND filing. Harbour expects to hold equity in both Spruce and Adrenyx after a pro rata distribution of Adrenyx shares to Spruce shareholders. The asset was licensed by Harbour incubator HBMAT to Spruce in 2025 for territories outside Greater China.
items.src: Harbour BioMed press release via PR Newswire (2026-11-17)
items.author: InLight Editorial

items.t: Marrow Therapeutics launches with $173M in Series A and B financing
items.ms: A $53 million Series A was co-led by Scion Life Sciences and venBio; a $120 million Series B was led by OrbiMed, with RTW, Surveyor, KKR and others participating.
items.why: On November 17, 2026, Watertown-based Marrow Therapeutics launched with a transferrin-receptor (TfR1)–directed antibody-conjugate platform aimed at the bone marrow. Its lead candidate, MAR-101, is in IND-enabling preparation and is designed to lower BCL11a and reactivate fetal hemoglobin for sickle cell disease and beta-thalassemia.
items.author: InLight Editorial

items.t: FDA launches Global Reliance Disclosure Program to share redacted approval reviews with foreign regulators
items.ms: The program began on October 30 with a temporary PEPFAR-related approval of lenacapavir and is currently limited in scope. FDA intends to expand it in January 2027 to all new-molecular-entity NDAs and 351(a) biologics license applications.
items.why: On November 17, 2026, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration announced the Global Reliance Disclosure Program (GRDP), which lets applicants, after approval, request minimally redacted FDA review materials for submission to foreign regulators, so those agencies can take FDA's review into account and reduce duplicative evaluation. No deal value was disclosed.
items.author: InLight Editorial

items.t: Johnson & Johnson to acquire Ollin Biosciences; lead asset is Innovent-originated IBI324
items.ms: $2.2 billion upfront, plus up to about $1.125 billion in regulatory and sales milestones; closing is expected before the end of 2026, subject to approvals and customary conditions. Innovent's verified release does not disclose what share of proceeds it would receive as licensor.
items.why: On November 16, 2026, Johnson & Johnson agreed to acquire Ollin Biosciences. Ollin's lead candidate, OLN324, is the VEGF/Ang2 bispecific antibody IBI324, which Innovent invented and licensed to Ollin; global Phase 3 enrollment is underway in diabetic macular edema and wet age-related macular degeneration. After closing, Blackstone Life Sciences will pay Johnson & Johnson a total of $750 million in installments to fully fund OLN324's Phase 3 development, in return for certain milestones and a single-digit royalty.
items.src: Johnson & Johnson press release (2026-11-16); Innovent press release (2026-11-16)
items.author: InLight Editorial

items.t: Lilly agrees to acquire Calytrix Bio for up to $1.5B in cash; upfront not separately disclosed
items.ms: Calytrix shareholders may receive up to $1.5 billion in cash, including an upfront payment and later clinical and regulatory milestones. The upfront amount was not separately disclosed.
items.why: On November 16, 2026, privately held Calytrix Bio announced an agreement to be acquired by Eli Lilly. Its lead program is a biparatopic antibody directed at mutant calreticulin (mCALR)–driven essential thrombocythemia and myelofibrosis, and is still preclinical.
items.src: Calytrix Bio press release via PR Newswire (2026-11-16)
items.author: InLight Editorial

items.t: Seawolf Therapeutics debuts with $100M in financing and a Sanofi collaboration
items.ms: Combined seed and Series A financing of $100 million. A multi-target research collaboration and exclusive license with Sanofi, covering bleeding disorders and other undisclosed indications, includes up to $1.2 billion in milestones plus tiered royalties; the upfront was not disclosed.
items.why: On November 16, 2026, San Diego-based Seawolf Therapeutics launched. Investors include Versant, MPM BioImpact, Novartis Venture Fund, Lilly and CRISPR Therapeutics. Its platform is TRIDENT, a redosable LNP DNA delivery system.
items.author: InLight Editorial

items.t: Sinotau-B (09941.HK) opens Hong Kong IPO; trading expected November 24
items.ms: The company plans a global offering of 6.561 million H shares at HK$52.0–68.0, for total proceeds of about HK$341.17 million to HK$446.15 million, excluding any greenshoe. The offer runs November 16–19, with trading expected to start at 9:00 a.m. on November 24.
items.why: Beijing Sinotau is a radiopharmaceutical company. Its core products include XTR008, a late-stage 177Lu-labeled SSTR radioligand, and XTR004, a myocardial perfusion imaging agent already in Phase 3.
items.author: InLight Editorial

items.t: Phrontline Biopharma raises about $40M in a Series A
items.ms: The round was jointly led by YuanBio Venture Capital and Decheng Capital. The company says this follows a $60 million Pre-A+ in November 2025, bringing the two rounds to nearly $100 million in a year.
items.why: Proceeds will support clinical work and INDs for bispecific and dual-payload ADC programs, including EGFR×B7-H3 ADC TJ101, which reported Phase 1a data at ESMO 2026, and FRα×CDH6 dual-payload ADC TJ102, which the company describes as the first of its kind to enter the clinic.
items.author: InLight Editorial

items.t: FDA Issues Complete Response Letter for Ivonescimab in EGFR-Mutated NSCLC After TKI Therapy
items.ms: FDA issued a CRL; HARMONi met its PFS endpoint, but the primary OS analysis did not reach statistical significance.
items.why: On November 15, 2026, Summit Therapeutics announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued a Complete Response Letter (CRL) for the biologics license application (BLA) for ivonescimab plus platinum-containing chemotherapy. The application cannot be approved in its present form. Ivonescimab is a PD-1 × VEGF bispecific antibody invented by Akeso (HKEX: 09926); Summit holds rights in the United States and other licensed territories. The sought indication is locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) in patients who have received prior epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) therapy.
items.author: InLight Editorial

items.t: China releases the 2026 NRDL and commercial innovative-drug list, effective January 1, 2027
items.ms: The basic medical-insurance list adds 107 drugs, including 51 Class 1 innovative drugs, and removes 34. The commercial innovative-drug list adds 12 products, bringing the total to 28; two 2025 commercial-list products move into the basic list.
items.why: The notice is dated November 13, 2026, and was posted on the National Healthcare Security Administration website on November 14. A State Council digest said that lymphoma CAR-T and non-factor hemophilia therapies that previously cost more than RMB 1 million have been added to the basic list. Products on the commercial innovative-drug list are not paid from the basic pooling fund; placement in hospitals is, in principle, to follow the rules used for negotiated drugs.
items.src: National Healthcare Security Administration notice (2026-11-14); gov.cn digest (2026-11-16)
items.author: InLight Editorial

items.t: RemeGen amends its Vor Bio license to add RC298, with about $56M in upfront value
items.ms: RemeGen will receive about $56 million in upfront value ($10 million cash plus warrants to buy 2.3 million Vor Bio shares, valued at about $46 million on the November 11 close, with an exercise price of $0.0001 a share) and up to $300 million in development milestones, including $20 million tied to early clinical development and tech transfer.
items.why: The agreement was signed on November 12 and announced on November 13. Vor Bio receives exclusive rights to develop and commercialize the long-acting BAFF/APRIL inhibitor RC298 outside Greater China; RemeGen keeps Greater China rights and will continue to lead preclinical and Phase 1 work in China. Sales milestones and royalties follow the original telitacicept license, calculated on aggregate net sales of all licensed products. RC298 is still preclinical and being prepared for an IND.
items.src: RemeGen company announcement, via Shanghai Securities News / Sina Finance (2026-11-13)
items.author: InLight Editorial

items.t: Windward Bio lists on Nasdaq (WWB); IPO and concurrent Sanofi placement expected to raise $225M
items.ms: The company priced 10,294,117 shares at $17.00 each and placed $50 million privately with Sanofi. It said the IPO and concurrent private placement are expected to raise $225 million in total, excluding any underwriter option.
items.why: The offering was priced on November 12, with trading beginning November 13. Basel-based Windward's lead program, WIN378, a long-acting anti-TSLP antibody, originated in a Harbour BioMed–Kelun-Biotech collaboration; WIN027 originated at Yumab. Both licenses cover territories outside Greater China and certain other Asian markets. A November 16 release from investor Pivotal bioVenture Partners China said the shares rose 68% on the first day, implying a market value of about $1.69 billion.
items.src: Windward Bio pricing announcement, GlobeNewswire (2026-11-12); Pivotal bioVenture Partners China press release (2026-11-16)
items.author: InLight Editorial

items.t: US Defense Department removes WuXi AppTec from the Section 1260H list, without ruling out relisting
items.ms: The Federal Register published the removal notice on November 10. The notice is dated November 5 and does not separately specify an effective date.
items.why: The Defense Department removed WuXi AppTec from its list of Chinese military companies operating in the United States in compliance with an August 7 preliminary injunction issued by the US District Court for the District of Columbia. The injunction bars enforcing or giving effect to WuXi AppTec's Section 1260H designation. The notice expressly preserves the possibility of relisting on additional or supplementary grounds. This change concerns a specific list and should not be read as lifting other US restrictions or procurement rules; no deal value was disclosed.
items.src: US Department of Defense, Federal Register notice 2026-22840 (2026-11-10)
items.author: InLight Editorial

items.t: China's health and insurance authorities outline measures to improve hospital access to innovative drugs
items.ms: Four authorities jointly issued a notice on the safe, rational provision and use of innovative drugs; no transaction value was disclosed.
items.why: Xinhua reported on November 10 that China's National Health Commission, National Healthcare Security Administration, National Administration of Traditional Chinese Medicine and National Disease Control and Prevention Administration issued the notice. Hospitals at secondary level and above are asked to streamline formulary review and add relevant innovative drugs according to clinical needs and capabilities. Measures cover prescribing and reimbursement training, pharmacy-service pricing, removal of limits on total formulary variety and specifications, and exclusion of certain innovative drugs from specified per-visit and per-admission drug-cost growth performance metrics. The report did not announce release dates for new reimbursement or commercial-insurance drug lists.
items.src: Xinhua report (2026-11-10); based on a news report
items.author: InLight Editorial

items.t: BRL Medicine completes another equity round, saying 2026 rounds now exceed RMB 700M
items.ms: The company said that after this round, its two 2026 equity financings together exceed RMB 700 million. The release does not state this round's amount or name the investors.
items.why: Proceeds will support clinical development, regulatory filings and industrialization of core products, including BRL-101, a gene-edited hematopoietic stem-cell product that has met the primary endpoint in a pivotal study in transfusion-dependent beta-thalassemia, and allogeneic CD19 CAR-T BRL-303 (Phase 1 in SLE ongoing; SSc has received implied CDE clearance).
items.author: InLight Editorial

items.t: Alphana Therapeutics completes the first close of a $50M Series A
items.ms: The $50 million round's first close was led by Guozhong Capital, with participation from the Hefei industrial-investment system and others.
items.why: The report is dated November 6, 2026. Proceeds will support in vivo CAR-T, cancer-vaccine and other pipeline programs, as well as the TALENT platform.
items.author: InLight Editorial

items.t: Sino Biopharm grants Boehringer Ingelheim options on six preclinical ADC and T-cell engager programs
items.ms: $358 million in upfront and near-term payments, up to $7.0 billion in option-exercise, development, regulatory and commercial milestones, and royalties up to a double-digit percentage. Five programs come from LaNova Medicines and one from Beijing Tide Pharmaceutical; on exercise Boehringer gains rights outside mainland China, Hong Kong and Macau for four programs and global rights for two.
items.why: Sino Biopharm leads early development through global Phase 1; this is the companies' second oncology collaboration.

items.t: Hinova licenses VAV1 molecular glue degrader HP570 to Evommune (ex-Greater China)
items.ms: $30 million non-refundable upfront ($20 million cash plus $10 million in Evommune warrants), up to $1.07 billion in development, regulatory and commercial milestones, and tiered royalties on net sales outside Greater China.
items.why: Evommune (internal code EVO570) plans a mid-stage study in rheumatoid arthritis in 2027, per Reuters.
items.src: Hinova announcement via Xinhua Finance (2026-11-05); Reuters (2026-11-04)

items.t: Minghui licenses Japan rights to subcutaneous IGF-1R antibody MHB018A to ASKA
items.ms: $110 million upfront, up to $330 million in development, regulatory and commercial milestones, and tiered royalties up to the mid-30% range on Japan net sales. Minghui keeps all rights outside Japan and leads global development.
items.why: MHB018A is being developed for thyroid eye disease; Minghui is running four Phase 3 studies (two in China, two global).

items.t: CStone partners with Kimia to lead Phase 1 of a DDR-pathway small molecule
items.ms: CStone leads Phase 1 (dose escalation and expansion in biomarker-selected patients) in mainland China and Australia; Kimia pays the related clinical development costs. CStone is entitled to milestones and royalties on global net sales during the royalty term. Amounts were not disclosed.
items.why: The solid-tumor candidate was discovered on Kimia's ATLAS platform, which combines AI with automated synthesis and screening.

items.t: FDA grants priority review to BeOne's zanubrutinib plus rituximab in first-line mantle cell lymphoma
items.ms: FDA accepted the supplemental new drug application and granted priority review; the first-line indication is not yet approved.
items.why: According to BeOne's press release, the randomized Phase 3 MANGROVE trial enrolled 510 previously untreated adults with mantle cell lymphoma. Zanubrutinib plus rituximab reduced the risk of progression or death by 43% versus bendamustine plus rituximab (HR 0.57; 95% CI 0.43–0.76; p<0.0001), meeting the primary endpoint of independently reviewed progression-free survival. The company reported no new safety signals and plans to present full results at ASH on December 13. Priority review does not guarantee approval.
items.src: BeOne Medicines press release via Business Wire (2026-11-03); based on a press release
items.author: InLight Editorial

items.t: Boan Biotech licenses denosumab biosimilar BA6101 (60 mg) for Japan
items.ms: The partner gains exclusive commercialisation rights in Japan; Boan receives an upfront payment, milestones and royalties. Amounts and partner were not disclosed.
items.why: The reference product Pralia had 2025 sales in Japan of JPY45.8 billion (+8.3% year on year), per the announcement.

items.t: Pelthos to combine with Castle Creek Biosciences (D-Fi)
items.ms: Castle Creek holders receive 5.2 million Pelthos shares (~32.5% fully diluted), up to 5.8 million more on FDA approval of D-Fi, up to $300 million in milestones (including $50 million on specified Phase 3 endpoints) and 80% of net proceeds from any priority review voucher.
items.why: Expected to close by the end of Q1 2027, subject to Castle Creek stockholder approval.

items.t: Junshi doses first patient in Phase 3 of JS207 plus JS007 for first-line HCC
items.ms: The randomized Phase 3 compares PD-1/VEGF bispecific JS207 plus anti-CTLA-4 JS007 with toripalimab plus bevacizumab. In earlier data, ORR was 44.1% and DCR 85.3% among 34 evaluable patients.

items.t: Hisun Pharma in-licenses Xuanjing Bio siRNA platform and RGN6669
items.ms: Upfront payment of RMB10 million; development milestones up to RMB348 million and sales milestones up to RMB630 million.
items.why: The deal covers cardiovascular, metabolic and respiratory targets. It requires approval at the extraordinary general meeting on 12 November 2026.
items.src: Zhejiang Hisun Pharmaceutical announcement Lin 2026-78 via SSE (2026-10-28)

items.t: NMPA converts Junshi toripalimab urothelial cancer indication to full approval
items.ms: Monotherapy for locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma after platinum chemotherapy moved from conditional to regular approval, based mainly on the RC48-C016 study (NCT05302284).

items.t: Alphamab doses first patient in Phase 3 of JSKN033 for cervical cancer
items.ms: JSKN033 (subcutaneous HER2 bispecific ADC + PD-L1 inhibitor combination) is tested as monotherapy in recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer after platinum chemotherapy and PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors.

items.t: Ferring agrees to acquire fertility biotech Gameto
items.ms: Deal value of up to $1.3825 billion, subject to development, regulatory and commercial milestones; closing remains subject to conditions.
items.why: Gameto’s In Vitro Maturation programme is investigational in the US and not FDA-approved.

items.t: Duality/BioNTech DYNASTY-Breast02 meets PFS primary endpoint
items.ms: At interim analysis, the trastuzumab pamirtecan (DB-1303/BNT323) arm showed a statistically significant, modest PFS improvement over chemotherapy in 541 HR+/HER2-low patients; OS is immature. ILD incidence was higher than in prior trials, mostly grade 1–2.
items.why: The company states the potential clinical benefit for this population may be relatively limited; the partners will analyse the data further.

items.t: Baicheng Pharma and related party Zhiyao Technology form joint venture Hangzhou Baijing Bio
items.ms: The joint venture has registered capital of RMB20 million: Baicheng contributes RMB14 million (70%) and Zhiyao Technology RMB6 million (30%); once established it will be a controlled subsidiary of Baicheng.
items.why: Baicheng Pharma plans to set up a new company, Hangzhou Baijing Biotechnology Co., Ltd. (provisional name), with its related party Shenzhen Zhiyao Technology. It combines Baicheng's CRO/CDMO industrialisation and clinical development experience with Zhiyao's technology in AI-driven molecular design and intelligent crystal-form and formulation development, and will handle pipeline R&D, external financing, patent licensing, asset transactions and later commercialisation. Baicheng non-independent director Jiang Yide is also a director of Zhiyao Technology, so the deal is a related-party transaction; the board approved it on 23 October 2026, and it does not need shareholder approval.

items.t: CSPC starts China phase 3 of B7-H3 ADC SYS6043 in first-line triple-negative breast cancer
items.ms: Randomised, open-label, multicentre phase 3: SYS6043 versus investigator's choice of chemotherapy as first-line treatment for unresectable recurrent or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer; the first study site has been initiated.
items.why: In a voluntary HKEX announcement, CSPC describes SYS6043 as a B7-H3-targeted antibody-drug conjugate whose linker-payload is a tetrapeptide linker conjugated to a topoisomerase I inhibitor; protease cleavage releases the payload, which has a bystander effect. The announcement says its Fc design can reduce lymphocyte uptake and lower the risk of off-target toxicity. The phase 3 has started at the first site in China, and recruitment and screening are under way. No amount was disclosed; efficacy awaits the trial results.

items.t: HUTCHMED's ex-China licence of a KRAS-EGFR conjugate to GSK closes
items.ms: $110M upfront (expected shortly); up to $1.185B in regulatory, development and commercial sales milestones; plus tiered royalties on net sales.
items.why: HUTCHMED announced that its exclusive development and licence agreement with a GSK affiliate for HMPL-A830 has closed after antitrust review and other closing conditions were met. GSK obtains worldwide rights outside mainland China, Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan. HMPL-A830 is an antibody-targeted therapy conjugate (ATTC) that links a small-molecule KRAS inhibitor payload to an anti-EGFR antibody; a phase 1a trial started in September 2026 (NCT07718581). HUTCHMED is responsible for global phase 1 development, and GSK for later development and commercialisation in its territory.

items.t: Zelgen receives first $10M milestone payment from AbbVie for ZG006
items.ms: A $10M near-term milestone tied to clinical-trial progress, after a $100M upfront received earlier. The agreement also includes up to $60M in near-term milestone and option-related payments, up to $1.075B in milestones, and tiered royalties.
items.why: Zelgen and AbbVie signed a global strategic collaboration and option-to-license agreement for ZG006 (alveltamig) on 30 December 2025: AbbVie obtains exclusive development and commercialisation rights outside Greater China, and Zelgen keeps Greater China. The announcement says Zelgen received the $100 million upfront at the start of the year and has now received a $10 million near-term milestone from AbbVie based on clinical-trial progress. Net sales outside Greater China carry tiered royalties from high single digits to mid-double digits.

items.t: Sino Biopharm completes enrollment in phase 3 of TSLP antibody TQC2731 for nasal polyps
items.ms: The registrational phase 3 of TQC2731 as maintenance treatment for chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP) has completed enrollment; a phase 3 in severe asthma is ongoing.
items.why: TQC2731, developed in-house by Sino Biopharm subsidiary Chia Tai Tianqing, is a humanised monoclonal antibody against TSLP. TSLP is an epithelium-derived upstream inflammatory signal, and the announcement argues that blocking it may regulate both type 2 and non-type 2 inflammation; existing biologics mostly target type 2 inflammation, and CRSwNP still recurs after surgery in 35%–60% of patients. The announcement calls TQC2731 the first China-developed TSLP antibody to reach phase 3. No amount was disclosed; efficacy awaits the phase 3 results.

items.t: CSPC starts China phase 1 of SYH2083, a dual LFA-1/RASP eye drop for dry eye disease
items.ms: Phase 1 (SYH2083-001): single-centre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled dose escalation evaluating the safety, tolerability and pharmacokinetics of single and multiple doses in healthy Chinese participants.
items.why: In a voluntary HKEX announcement, CSPC describes SYH2083 eye drops as a dual inhibitor of lymphocyte function-associated antigen 1 (LFA-1) and reactive aldehyde species (RASP): it blocks the LFA-1–ICAM-1 interaction and reduces LFA-1-mediated cell adhesion while trapping reactive aldehydes. The company expects the two targets to act together and overcome limitations of single-target drugs. The phase 1 has started in China, and recruitment and screening are under way. No amount was disclosed.

items.t: Hansoh and Roche sign an ADC strategic collaboration and licence agreement
items.ms: $400M upfront plus a $110M first-anniversary payment; potential milestones of more than $15B; tiered royalties. Closing is subject to customary conditions including expiry of the HSR waiting period.
items.why: Hansoh and Roche signed on 17 October 2026. The collaboration covers a set of ADC programmes: two Hansoh preclinical ADCs and several programmes built on Hansoh's ADC platform against targets proposed by Roche. Hansoh leads early development, at the latest through completion of global phase 1a; Roche is responsible for later development outside mainland China, Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan, where Hansoh keeps all rights. Hansoh may opt into overseas development of up to two programmes and receive additional economics on their US commercialisation. The milestone figure is a nominal cap tied to agreed conditions; whether it is paid depends on programmes advancing.

items.t: FDA grants accelerated approval to GSK's Jemperli for MSI-H/dMMR locally advanced rectal cancer
items.ms: FDA accelerated approval of dostarlimab (Jemperli) for adults with stage II–III MSI-H/dMMR locally advanced rectal cancer, based on the phase 2 AZUR-1 trial.
items.why: GSK disclosed in a Form 6-K filed with the SEC that the FDA approved Jemperli under the accelerated approval pathway for stage II–III MSI-H/dMMR locally advanced rectal cancer, which the company calls the first immunotherapy approved in this indication. In AZUR-1 the investigator-assessed 12-month sustained clinical complete response rate was 68% (98/144); the independent central review data for the primary objective are still maturing (47%, 54/116). With median follow-up of more than two years, no recurrences were reported among responders. Serious adverse reactions occurred in 20% of patients. The approval means some patients may avoid chemotherapy, radiotherapy and surgery, but it requires biomarker testing at diagnosis.

items.t: Estuary Bio raises $103M to advance local AAV therapy for ADPKD
items.ms: $93M Series A led by RA Capital plus a $10M seed co-led by 4BIO and GV; $103M in total
items.why: Estuary is developing local AAV gene therapy for autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease, from the Somlo and Caplan labs at Yale. EST-201 targets PKD2 and is slated for the clinic in 2027; EST-101 targets PKD1 and is slated for 2028. The $103 million total comprises a $93 million Series A led by RA Capital and a $10 million seed co-led by 4BIO and GV.

items.t: AstraZeneca and insitro form a strategic collaboration in difficult-to-treat cardiometabolic disease
items.ms: $40M upfront; up to about $1.46B in milestones; single-digit royalties; AstraZeneca takes exclusive worldwide rights to selected programmes
items.why: The collaboration covers metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) and cardiomyopathies and runs on insitro's Virtual Human platform. AstraZeneca pays $40 million up front, with up to about $1.46 billion in milestones and single-digit royalties, and takes exclusive worldwide rights to selected programmes. The milestone figure is a nominal cap tied to agreed conditions, not a valuation or expected revenue; everything beyond the upfront depends on programmes advancing.

items.t: OMass Therapeutics raises a $310M Series C
items.ms: $310M (GBP230M) Series C, co-led by Bain Capital Life Sciences, Forbion and Novo Holdings
items.why: The round funds a small-molecule portfolio in endocrinology and immunology: it will take OMS1620, an MC2R antagonist, through phase 2 development in congenital adrenal hyperplasia and ACTH-dependent Cushing's syndrome, and generate initial clinical data for an SLC15A4 inhibitor for lupus. The $310 million (GBP230 million) financing was co-led by Bain Capital Life Sciences, Forbion and Novo Holdings.

items.t: City Therapeutics prices upsized IPO at about $200M
items.ms: 11,111,111 shares at $18 for about $200M; expected to begin trading on Nasdaq as CTY on Oct 16, closing expected Oct 19
items.why: The company sold 11,111,111 shares at $18 each for roughly $200 million in an upsized offering. The stock was expected to begin trading on Nasdaq under CTY on 16 October 2026, with closing expected on 19 October. The announcement names CITY-FXI, CITY-RBP4 and CITY-TFR2 among its programmes.

items.t: CSPC announces China IND for SYS6088, a PD-1/VEGFA/CTLA-4 trispecific
items.ms: NMPA clinical trial approval in advanced or metastatic solid tumours; PD-1/VEGFA/CTLA-4 trispecific antibody with an engineered Fc
items.why: CSPC's voluntary HKEX announcement describes SYS6088 as a PD-1/VEGFA/CTLA-4 trispecific antibody with an engineered Fc, and says China's NMPA has approved it for clinical trials in advanced or metastatic solid tumours. No deal value is attached; clinical benefit will depend on trial data still to come.
